claims.text: The completed trip ran 16.2 km against the booked optimal of 12.0 km - an excess of 4.2 km, or 35% - so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass at once: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal (2.4 km) and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The distance figure is taken from the trace, which POL-RD-01 makes the governing field over the rounded trip_record copy, and here the trace reports the same 16.2 km. A route deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

The trace this finding rests on is clean: 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0, so no limb of POL-RD-07 fires - there is no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m between consecutive fixes, and no sustained interval above 30 seconds. No impairment discount or independent-corroboration requirement applies to this ride.

No exculpatory closure can be raised against this route. The only traffic advisory artifact is MISSING: it carries no payload and weight 0.0, so there is no advisory naming any road, expressway segment or junction the optimal route traverses, and POL-RD-03 cannot be run. The absence itself is citable, and it leaves the detour entirely unexplained.

The detour was not rider-caused. The chat log holds exactly two messages, neither with a waypoint_hint and neither naming a road or a place, and the rider's own message at 08:12:00 asked the driver to return to the booked route after Pioneer Road. With no actionable rider instruction and no requested waypoint, the POL-RD-04 exoneration is unavailable on this record and the driver's assertion that 'the rider did not request any stop' is beside the point.

There was no relocation of either endpoint. On the trip record pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are all null, so POL-RD-05 has nothing to re-apply and the booked 12.0 km optimal stands as the POL-RD-01 baseline.

This is not a pooled trip, so no part of the excess can be excused as co-rider collection. The vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null; POL-RD-12 does not apply and the 12.0 km booked optimal governs without adjustment.

On this METERED fare the POL-RD-02 recomputation is arithmetic, not discretion: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x the 1.2 surge multiplier recorded on the FARE_BREAKDOWN) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the on-route gantry - 1.00 promo discount = 24.2240. The refund is charged_total 33.36 - 24.2240 = 9.1360, rounded UP to 9.15. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of 9.15 - exactly the contested amount.

The 2.00 Tuas South Avenue 8 loop ERP line must not be added on top of that 9.15. Under POL-RD-09(1) off-route ERP is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare carries only the 1.00 Pioneer Road inbound gantry that lies on the optimal route; the 2.00 is itemised for transparency and is returned inside the 9.15, and adding it again would be the exact double count the clause forbids.

Setting the money aside, the Tuas South Avenue 8 loop line is a billing-integrity concern the ruling should record. That gantry carries on_optimal_route false, its nearest trace fix is 1,645.7 m away, no fix falls within the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 sets for a crossing, and no gap brackets the closest approach - the rider was charged 2.00 for a gantry the trace never passes. I claim no separate sum for it, because the line is already returned inside the POL-RD-02 refund, but POL-RD-09(4) directs that an unmatched charge line be recorded as a billing-integrity finding and referred.

The rider has carried her initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip TRP-09111, and the excess that clears the POL-RD-01 threshold is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, and his counterparty statement names no artifact and no clause - it is a general assertion that carries no weight on its own, while the trace places the vehicle off the booked corridor from about 08:05 onward with no return.

No extra corroboration is demanded of this claim. The rider_profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0 - nowhere near the 4-claim threshold - so the POL-RD-08 rider-reputation condition does not fire and the trace alone proves the excess.

The rider is the filing party and the fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so PARTIAL_REFUND is a rider win on POL-GEN-03's party-relative reading: it returns 9.15 of the charge the detour generated and leaves the rider not carrying the disputed amount.

I do not claim the POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation uplift, and the record does not support it: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610, which reaches neither the 3-flag count nor the 0.05 ratio, so no pattern is established and I draw no adverse inference from the driver's profile. The claim stands, as it must under POL-GEN-01, on this trip's own trace.

claims.text: POL-RD-01 sets two gates for establishment and a separate, higher gate for materiality. On this record the governing trace distance is 16.2 km against a booked optimal of 12.0 km: an excess of 4.2 km, or 35.00%. That clears the establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but falls well short of the material gate, which requires an excess over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km. The deviation is therefore established but NOT material, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, no FULL_REFUND of charged_total is licensed on this trip, and no driver-conduct referral arises.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, the only two counters that clause permits show no pattern at all: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the threshold of 3, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610 is 0, below the 0.05 ratio with the 40-trip floor. No repeat-deviation pattern is established. Under POL-GEN-01 the driver's remaining profile fields - prior_deviation_flags, rating, lifetime_trips, acceptance_rate - are context only and may not ground any adverse finding; prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure this test names.

The fare model recorded on the breakdown is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs: the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. Charged_total of 33.36 less recomputed_fare of 24.224 gives 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of charged_total, far below the 90% share that would substitute a FULL_REFUND, and far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis. The ceiling on the rider's recovery is therefore a PARTIAL_REFUND of 9.15 and nothing more.

The rider's complaint about an 'extra ERP charge' is answered by POL-RD-09(1), the anti-double-count rule. The 2.00 Tuas South Avenue 8 loop gantry is off the optimal route and is already comprehended inside the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputation credits only gantries lying on the optimal route. That charge may be itemised separately for transparency, but it must never be added on top of the 9.15 figure, and no separate pass-through refund is due on it.

The 1.00 Pioneer Road inbound gantry is flagged on_optimal_route true on the fare breakdown and is a properly chargeable pass-through line lying on the booked optimal corridor (the routing snapshot is 'via Pioneer Road and Tuas South Avenue 3'). It is correctly retained inside the recomputed fare of 24.224 and is not refundable to the rider under POL-RD-09.

I do not press a closure or rider-request exoneration, because the record does not carry one. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING - it has no payload, carries weight 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so no advisory names a segment the optimal route traverses. The driver's statement that he 'followed the road available to me' is the kind of general assertion that POL-RD-08 says cannot discharge the burden without a traffic_advisory ID, and no chat message from the rider requests a detour (waypoint_hint is null on both messages). The driver's case therefore rests on capping the remedy under POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02 and POL-RD-09, not on defeating the claim.

The trace is clean (205 fixes, 10-second interval, max_gap_sec 0, no gaps), so POL-RD-07 imposes no corroboration requirement and the excess is measured on the trace itself.

POL-RD-04 fails — the chat log holds no rider instruction carrying a waypoint_hint or naming a road, and the rider's own message asked the driver to return to the booked route. POL-RD-05 fails — neither endpoint was amended. POL-RD-12 fails — vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL.

The fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15, which is the contested amount.

The 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' ERP line is NOT added on top: the recomputed fare already credits only the 1.00 on-optimal Pioneer Road gantry, so the 2.00 is returned inside the 9.15 (POL-RD-09(1)) and adding it again would be the double count that limb forbids. Both profiles were used as credibility weighting only (POL-GEN-01); no adverse finding rests on rating, lifetime counters or any other context-only field. ruling.explanation:

THE DEVIATION. The GPS trace is clean — 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0 — so no limb of POL-RD-07 fires: no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval over 30 seconds, and no impairment discount or extra corroboration is required. Measured on the trace (16.2 km) against the booked optimal (12.0 km), the trip was 4.2 km longer, or 35.00%. That clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (over 20% of optimal and over 0.8 km) but falls short of its materiality gate (over 50% or over 8.0 km). The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED and NOT MATERIAL. Both advocates agree on this and I accept it.

NO UPLIFT, NO CONDUCT REFERRAL. Because the deviation is not material, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip's own evidence, so there is no FULL_REFUND of the whole fare and no driver-conduct referral. I have also run the POL-RD-06 pattern test: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 (below 3) and 0 divided by completed_trips_90d of 610 is 0 (below 0.05), so no repeat-deviation pattern is established. The rider's profile condition does not fire either: deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the 4-claim threshold in POL-RD-08, so no extra corroboration is demanded of the rider.

NO EXONERATION. There is no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is present but empty (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), so no advisory names a segment the optimal route traverses and POL-RD-03 cannot exonerate anything. The SGD 2.00 "Tuas South Avenue 8 loop" gantry is off the optimal route and is ALREADY comprehended inside the 9.15, because the recomputed fare counts only the SGD 1.00 "Pioneer Road inbound" gantry, which lies on the booked optimal corridor named in the trip record ("via Pioneer Road and Tuas South Avenue 3", with optimal_route_erp_sgd of 1.00). Treating it under POL-RD-09(4) is also why it does not force an escalation under POL-RD-10(8).
